q: Which layer of the OSI model is closest to the end user?
exp: The application layer provides network services directly to user applications.

q: Which IPv6 address prefix identifies link-local unicast addresses?
exp: Link-local addresses begin with FE80::/10; global unicast starts 2000::/3, multicast FF00::/8 and unique local FC00::/7.

q:
Statement I: OSPF routers flood link-state advertisements to build a view of the topology.
Statement II: RIP uses link bandwidth as its routing metric.
options: Statement I is true, Statement II is false
Statement I is false, Statement II is true
exp: OSPF is link-state with flooding; RIP uses hop count, not bandwidth, as its metric.

q: Which protocol provides the security layer used by HTTPS?
exp: HTTPS is HTTP carried over TLS (formerly SSL), providing encryption and authentication.

q: What is meant by piggybacking in the data link layer?
options: Combining several small packets into one
Attaching the acknowledgement to an outgoing data frame
exp: In piggybacking, the ACK for received data is carried in the header of the next data frame going the other way.

q: Which device has multiple interfaces, works at the network layer, and keeps each interface in a separate broadcast domain?
exp: Routers forward based on IP addresses and do not forward broadcasts, so each interface is its own broadcast domain.

q: A link has a raw bandwidth of 8 Mbps and the protocol overhead consumes 20% of the capacity. What is the effective throughput?
exp: Useful share is 80%: 0.8 × 8 = 6.4 Mbps.

q: A class B network with mask 255.255.252.0 is used. How many usable hosts does each subnet have?
exp: Mask 255.255.252.0 is /22, leaving 10 host bits: 2¹⁰ − 2 = 1022.

q: A TCP sender has cwnd = 32 MSS when a timeout occurs. What is the new value of ssthresh?
exp: On timeout ssthresh is set to half of the current cwnd, 32/2 = 16 MSS, and cwnd restarts from 1 MSS.

q: Data 10110 is to be sent using the CRC generator 1001 (x³ + 1). What CRC bits are appended?
exp: Dividing 10110000 by 1001 (mod-2) leaves remainder 100.

q: How does an Ethernet switch learn which stations are reachable through which port?
options: By examining the destination IP of frames
By examining the source MAC address of incoming frames
exp: A learning switch records the source MAC address and arrival port of each frame in its forwarding table.

q: Which technique assigns time slots dynamically only to those inputs that have data to send?
exp: Statistical TDM allocates slots on demand, so no capacity is wasted on idle inputs.

q: In CDMA, how are the signals of different users separated on the same frequency band?
exp: Each user's data is spread with a unique orthogonal code and recovered at the receiver by correlating with that code.

q: Light is confined inside an optical fibre core mainly because of:
exp: The core has a higher refractive index than the cladding, so light is guided by total internal reflection.

q: Which TCP/IP layer adds port numbers to the data received from the application?
exp: The transport layer (TCP/UDP) adds source and destination port numbers in its header.

q: Which technique allows many hosts with private addresses to share a single public IPv4 address?
exp: Network Address Translation rewrites private addresses (and ports) to a public address at the border router.

q: Router X is 2 hops-cost away from neighbour Y. Y advertises a distance of 5 to network Z. X currently has a distance of 9 to Z. After applying the distance vector update, what is X's distance to Z?
exp: New cost via Y = 2 + 5 = 7, which is less than 9, so X updates to 7.

q: After the third consecutive collision in Ethernet, a station chooses a random wait multiplier K from:
exp: After the nth collision K is chosen from 0 to 2ⁿ − 1; for n = 3 this is 0 to 7.

q: What is the correct order of messages in DHCP address assignment?
exp: The DORA sequence is Discover, Offer, Request, Acknowledge.

q: Which set of 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi channels (20 MHz wide) are non-overlapping?
exp: Channels 1, 6 and 11 are spaced at least 25 MHz apart and do not overlap.

q: In the Go-Back-N protocol the receiver window size is:
exp: A Go-Back-N receiver accepts only the next in-order frame, so its window size is 1.

q: One million bits are sent over a 2 Mbps link with a propagation delay of 20 ms. Ignoring other delays, how long until the last bit arrives?
exp: Transmission time = 10⁶ / 2×10⁶ = 0.5 s = 500 ms; adding 20 ms propagation gives 520 ms.

q: How many hexadecimal digits are there in a full IPv6 address (ignoring colons)?
exp: 128 bits / 4 bits per hex digit = 32 hexadecimal digits.

q: Silly window syndrome is a problem related to:
options: Flow control with very small window advertisements
exp: It arises when sender or receiver exchanges tiny segments because of small window updates, wasting bandwidth.

q: How many cable links are needed to connect 12 PCs in a star network through a central switch?
exp: Each PC has one link to the switch, so 12 links are needed.

q: A single parity bit can detect:
options: Any odd number of bit errors
Any even number of bit errors
exp: Any odd number of flipped bits changes the parity, but even numbers of flips cancel out and go undetected.

q: Which device performs modulation and demodulation of signals?
exp: A modem converts digital data to analog signals for transmission over telephone or cable lines and back again.

q: Network slicing, enabling multiple virtual networks over one physical infrastructure, is a key feature of which generation?
exp: Network slicing is a core capability of the 5G system architecture.

q: A network has addresses 192.168.0.0/24 and 192.168.1.0/24. Which single prefix summarises both?
exp: The two blocks differ only in the 24th bit, so combining them gives 192.168.0.0/23.

q: A cellular system has 140 channels in total and uses a cluster size of 7. How many channels are available in each cell?
exp: Channels per cell = total channels / cluster size = 140/7 = 20.

q:
Assertion (A): A router operates at the data link layer.
Reason (R): A router forwards packets using IP addresses.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
exp: Routers work at the network layer, so A is false; R is true because forwarding is based on IP addresses.

q: In the URL https://www.example.com:8080/index.html, what does 8080 represent?
exp: The number after the colon following the host name is the TCP port of the web server.

q: What is the purpose of the split horizon technique in distance vector routing?
options: To increase bandwidth for routing updates
To prevent routing loops by not advertising a route back out of the interface it was learned from
exp: Split horizon avoids advertising a route to the neighbour from which it was learned, reducing count-to-infinity loops.

q: In slotted ALOHA with an offered load G = 1 frame per slot, the throughput S = G·e^(−G) is approximately:
exp: S = 1 × e⁻¹ ≈ 0.368, which is also the maximum throughput of slotted ALOHA.

q: Which interframe space is the shortest in IEEE 802.11 DCF operation?
exp: SIFS is the shortest, giving highest priority to ACK, CTS and similar frames; the order is SIFS < PIFS < DIFS < EIFS.
